lessons.title: Rugs and migration functions
lessons.content:
# Rugs and migration functions

A rug is not a mood. It is a function that moves the pile to someone who is not you, faster than you can burn LP or withdraw shares. The polite name on many ABIs is **migrate**, **emergencyWithdraw**, **setFee**, **pause**, or `transferOwnership`. The impolite name is the same function after the admin uses it.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to spot migration, fee-to-100, and owner-pull patterns as rugs with ABIs, and refuse a “we migrated to v2” sentence without a named, verified destination you chose

## Liquidity that can walk

On many pairs the deployer still holds a large LP share, or a locker they control. Burning or transferring that LP drains reserves. “Locked” you already know to read. Unlocked LP in a deployer wallet is a gun with the safety off.

A **migration** function on a vault or a farm can move underlying to a new address. Sometimes that is a real upgrade. Sometimes the new address is a wallet. The ABI does not blush. You read `migrate(address)` and you ask who may call it.

## Fees that flip

A token or a pair with `setFee` can move a 0.3% fee to 99% on the way out. That is a rug that still looks like a swap. Combined with a delay on sells, it is a honeypot (next lesson). The parameter was always there. The poster showed 0.3%.

## Worked migrate

Farm v1: `migrate(newChef)`. Owner calls it with newChef = an EOA. LP that users staked is pulled to the EOA. Users still see a UI. Withdraw reverts or returns 0. Explorers show the call. Support says “new farm, approve this.” The second approve is the second gun.

A legitimate migrate names a verified new contract, a timelock, and a period when both can be read. Even then it is a trust event. This school does not assign you to follow a migrate. It assigns: a migrate exists or it does not. That is a yes/no on the ABI, not a vibe about the team’s “journey.”

## What to read without depositing

Owner, pending owner, timelock. Functions: migrate, pause, setFee, recoverToken, skim, mint. Whether LP is in a wallet. Whether the pair’s factory is known. You can do this on a contract you will never touch. Practising on a dead rug’s explorer page is safer than practising on a live one with size.

Crystal Stones verify-only still applies: reading CST’s extra functions is contract literacy. It is not a hunt for a CST farm to migrate into.

TABLE
Function | Looks like | Can be
migrate(address) | Upgrade | Send pile to an EOA
setFee | Parameter | 99% on sells
recoverToken | Rescue | Drain “stuck” user funds
pause | Safety | One-way door
transferOwnership | Ops | New finger on every gun
ENDTABLE

DIAGRAM
PILE
  |
  +-- owner LP (unlocked) --> burn/withdraw reserves
  +-- migrate(to) --> to is EOA?
  +-- setFee(99) --> sells die
Rug is a function, not a rumour.
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
If a poster says v2 without an address you typed from a calm bookmark, you do not have an upgrade. You have a request to follow a finger. Do not follow it as homework.
ENDNOTE

## Say this out loud

- Rugs are functions: migrate, setFee, owner LP.
- Unlocked deployer LP is a gun.
- “v2” needs a named contract.
- recoverToken can be a drain.
- No assigned migrate, no CST farm follow.

Next: Honeypots and tax flips.

lessons.title: Honeypots and tax flips
lessons.content:
# Honeypots and tax flips

A honeypot is a token you can buy and cannot usefully sell. The ABI may hide it as a tax, a blacklist, a max-tx, a trading flag, or a list of allowed sellers (the deployer). A **tax flip** is a honeypot with a delay: sells worked at 5% tax, then `setTax(99)` or `setTrading(false)` for everyone except a privileged address.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to name buy-ok/sell-fail patterns — tax, blacklist, max-tx, whitelist — and refuse a green candle on a token you have not tried to read as a seller

## How sells fail

**Blacklist / include-from.** Transfer reverts if `from` is you. **Tax on sell** so high that minOut cannot be met, or the router’s `transfer` of the token never delivers. **Max transaction** smaller than the pool’s advertised size so you can buy 10 and cannot sell 10. **Trading flag** only the owner can disable. **Whitelist of pairs** that can receive — your wallet is not on it.

Simulation tools exist. They are not assigned here as a vendor. The method is: read the extra functions, read who is excluded from tax, assume the excluded set is the house.

## The flip

Deployer sells into a rising candle while your sell is taxed 99%. Or trading is paused “for safety” after the pump. The candle was inventory leaving through a door you do not have. Reading `isExcludedFromFee(deployer)` after the fact is how you write the post-mortem. Reading it before would have been the lesson.

Some taxes fund “LP” that the owner can still pull. That is a rug plus a honeypot. Combined posters are common.

## Worked prompt

UI: buy TOKEN with 3% tax. You still do not buy — this school assigns no buy. On the read: `setTax`, `excludeFromFee`, `blacklist`, `maxTx`, `tradingOpen`. Owner is excluded. maxTx is 1% of supply but the owner’s max is unlimited. That is enough to stop. You do not need a sell-test with live money. The ABI already told you sells are a privilege.

## Green candles are not a counter-argument

A chart can print because the deployer is buying, because a bot is cycling, or because a few unlucky wallets bought. None of that is your exit. Honeypots need a chart. That is how they advertise.

CST as taught here is verify-only. This lesson does not claim CST is or is not a tax token; it claims you would read functions rather than a candle. Do not buy CST to test a sell. Do not buy anything to test a sell as academy work.

TABLE
Pattern | Buy | Sell
Blacklist | Often works | Reverts for you
99% sell tax | Works | Router cannot meet minOut
maxTx tiny | Small buy works | Your size reverts
Owner excluded | Owner can dump | You cannot
tradingOpen=false | Maybe not | No
ENDTABLE

DIAGRAM
CANDLE UP
    |
    +-- owner excluded from tax --> inventory leaving
    +-- you not excluded --> sell reverts or 99%
Read excludeFromFee before you invent a narrative.
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
A token that only the house can sell is not a market. It is a trap with a chart. This school will not send you in to “test the sell.”
ENDNOTE

## Say this out loud

- Honeypot: buy works, sell does not.
- Tax flips are delayed honeypots.
- Read who is excluded from fees.
- A candle is not an exit.
- No assigned buy-to-test-sell.

Next: Never-list for DeFi.

lessons.title: Never-list for DeFi
lessons.content:
# Never-list for DeFi

A never-list is not superstition. It is the set of signatures and objects this course has already named as how people lose inventory. You will not be graded for memorising a brand. You will be graded for refusing the pattern when it returns under a new logo.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to recite a DeFi never-list — unlimited unknown spenders, claim sites, CST as collateral, pasted routers, seeds, migrate-follows — and keep the yield box empty

## Never sign

Unlimited `approve` to a spender you met today. `permit` that names a token you actually value, on a site you opened from an airdrop. `setApprovalForAll` because a UI said “sign in.” A seed, a 2FA code, or a remote-desktop invite from anyone claiming academy staff or “vault support.” A transaction whose `to` is not you on a swap you thought was yours.

Never is operational. It is not a dare to do it with lab size. Lab size plus a max approve is how lab size becomes a story.

## Never treat as homework

A pair paste. A farm paste. A “lock LP 365.” A borrow. A loop. CST as collateral. CST as a swap. CST as a farm reward. A revoke helper from a social post the hour you panicked. A v2 migrate URL from a chat. A Mentor yield. Academy XP as APY.

You can write the quizzes without a live call. If you feel a quiz required a signature, the quiz is wrong.

## Never confuse objects

Router for pair. Pair for vault. Vault for farm. Farm for locker. Oracle for chart. Chart for fill. Fill for profit after fees. LP for original deposits. Emission APY for fee APY. Self-custody for no counterparty. Verified source for audit. Audit for safety. Safety for “cannot migrate.”

The mash is the injury. The never-list is mostly “do not mash.”

## Worked refusal

A card appears: “Official CST-USDT vault, 240% , approve to start Intermediate bonus.” You name the mash: CST is verify-only; Intermediate is not a vault; 240% is a poster; approve is a login; this school’s yield box is empty. You do not argue the APR. You close the card. That is the whole drill.

If the card is Mentor, it is a malfunction. If the card is a person claiming staff, it is an impostor. If the card is a website, it is a spender until a calm bookmark says otherwise — and even then this course still does not assign the deposit.

CST as collateral / farm / swap homework | Verify-only; not a desk
Pasted router or migrate | New spender / new pile destination
Borrow or loop as lab | Seize permission

ENDTABLE

NOTE
The never-list is the product of the course, restated as refusals. A certificate does not expire it.
ENDNOTE

## Say this out loud

- No unknown max approve.
- No airdrop claim sites.
- No seed, ever.
- No CST as collateral, farm, or swap homework.
- Empty yield box; no assigned borrow.

lessons.content:
# Close

You now have names: programs calling programs; vault, pool, router, oracle; allowance as login; constant product; minOut; collateral factor as seize permission; utilisation; LP as a share of now; 4× hold 5,000 versus pool 4,000; farms as extra keys; lock as a word; rugs as functions; honeypots as sell-fail. The close is to keep those names and leave the desks where they are.

By the end of this lesson you should be able to close the course with the refusals intact — empty yield box, no assigned borrow, CST verify-only — and treat a certificate as academic, not as an LP position

## What you can say without shaking

DeFi is bytecode calling bytecode. Self-custody is the key, not an empty room. Approvals are standing pull-rights. A swap is a curve plus a router plus a bound. A borrow is a permission to be liquidated. An LP token is a share of current reserves. IL at 4× is hold 5,000 versus pool 4,000 on the classic paper. Farms drip another token and want another approve. Lock, migrate, and tax are functions to read.

If you can say those sentences, you can refuse a poster that skips them.

## What you still will not do as academy work

You will not be told to buy, swap, LP, farm, lock, lend, or borrow. You will not be told to post Crystal Stones as collateral or to pay tuition in it. You will not be given a router to bless. You will not be given a revoke helper to trust because you panicked. The yield box stays empty. The borrow box stays empty.

A later Advanced track, if it exists, does not silently fill those boxes. Watch the live site you typed. Do not watch a chat for a sudden desk.

## Certificate, XP, Mentor

A certificate is academic. It is not a vault manager licence, not proof of LP, not a whitelist. XP is not emissions. Mentor is an in-app assistant. If it names a pair, an APY, a collateral, or an entry, that is a malfunction. Report it. Do not size it.

Staff will not ask for a seed to “finalise DeFi module 6.” Anyone who does is an impostor. Checkout rails were stated once in the first lesson. They have not changed because you reached Close.

## A last worked refusal

Someone you study with says, “We finished DeFi, let us LP the CST pair so the certificate means something.” You say: the certificate already means we can name machines. LP would mean we minted a share of a pile, took IL risk, granted a spender, and treated a verify-only token as a desk. That is not the close of this course. That is the start of a different, unassigned story.

Then you stop. The close is a stop, not a launch.

TABLE
Object | This course left you | This course did not leave you
Machines named | Yes | A farm
IL arithmetic | Yes, 5000 vs 4000 | An LP position
Allowance literacy | Yes | A blessed spender
Liquidation literacy | Yes | A debt
Certificate | Academic | A licence or a whitelist
ENDTABLE

DIAGRAM

CLOSE: same sentence, plus refusals
yield box empty
borrow box empty
CST verify-only
Mentor farm = malfunction
STOP, do not launch.
ENDDIAGRAM

NOTE
You are done when the refusals are boring. If they still feel like a missed farm, read module 1 again — not a pair.
ENDNOTE

## Say this out loud

- DeFi is programs calling programs.
- The yield box is empty.
- No assigned borrow; no CST as collateral.
- A certificate is not an LP.
- Mentor naming a farm is a malfunction.

Next: End of DeFi (Decentralized Finance).
